SST-Hydrogen: Short-Range Circulation Coupling (Deprecated as Gravity)
Omar Iskandarani *
July 9, 2026
}
Abstract. Canonical status (v0.6.1+): The additive-circulation/Bernoulli cross-term mechanism is retained here as ashort-range interaction model (pressure/flux coupling), but it isdeprecated as a long-range gravity mechanism. For vθ∝1/r, the interaction energy scales as Vint∝1/r2 and therefore the force scales as F∝1/r3, i.e. too steep for an inverse-square gravitational law. Long-range 1/r potentials in SST are modeled via a local mediator field obeying a Poisson equation on R3 (see Emergent Inverse-Square Law).

Chiral Swirling Knots and Central Holes

Consider a chiral knot K embedded in R3, such as Fig.~fig:knot-gallery:

Each knot can be parametrized on a torus with major radius R and minor radius r. The core tube of radius rc supports a tangential swirl velocity v↺, defining the Swirl Clock S(t)↺.

A key structural feature is a central hole threaded by a straight axis (taken as the z-axis), along which the analytic swirl potential is singular. {

Cauchy Integral and Circulation Quantization

Let C be a closed loop in the x–y plane encircling the z-axis. For an analytic swirl potential W(z)=Φ+iΨ in a simply connected region, (1)∮Cv↺⋅dl={0,if no singularity inside,2πiRes(dWdz,z=0),if the axis is enclosed. In SST we identify the residue with a circulation quantum κ. Independently of the complex-potential language, Kelvin’s theorem fixes circulation~[helmholtz1858], [kelvin1869], [Saffman1992], [MajdaBertozzi2002] on any material loop; both viewpoints agree on the integer plateau: (2)ΓC=nκif the loop links n times with the core.

Canonical identification of κ (SST)
We adopt the equivalence κ≡hmeff=2πrcvc which gives a direct bridge between the quantum of circulation and core kinematics. Hence meff=h2πrcvc.

Numerics (SI): with rc=1.40897017e−15m and vc=‖v↺‖=1.09384563e6m/s, κ=2πrcvc=9.6836192e−9m2/s,meff=hκ=6.842555e−26kg≈38.384GeV/c2.
Status/limits: Dimensions are consistent ([κ]=L2T−1). For loops whose spanning disk intersects the torus annulus of the filament, Γ plateaus at nκ; for loops entirely outside, Γ≈0 (as illustrated in Fig.~fig:trefoil_axis_plateau_clean).
Swirl–EM correspondence (operational note)
In the Canon’s swirl–EM mapping, time-varying core areal density acts as a “source” via a term of the form b↺=G↺∂tϱ↺, providing a handle for experimental couplings. Dynamics on the central line that modulate ϱ↺ can therefore seed measurable EM-like responses without curving space, consistent with the flat-space treatment used here.

Composite Baryon Tubes

Inside baryons, three quark knots (e.g., 52, 52, 61; see Figs.~fig:5-2 and fig:6-1) meet at a Y-shaped junction, forming a single composite swirl tube (Fig.~fig:three-knot-gallery).Each quark knot i has circulation Γi=κ around the central axis (Fig.~fig:baryon_composite_tube). By Kelvin’s theorem (linearity of circulation), (3)Γbaryon=Γ1+Γ2+Γ3=3κ. Since Γ=2πrvθ, (4)vθ,eff=Γbaryon2πreff=3κ2πreff, with reff the effective core radius of the merged tube. In the thin-core, near-Rankine limit reff≈rc to leading order (so that vθ,eff≈3vc holds as a first-order estimate), while the deeper pressure well is set by the increased Γ.
Swirl Clock scaling.

The Swirl Clock relation becomes (5)dtlocal=dt∞1−(3vc)2c2, predicting a more pronounced local time dilation, consistent with the larger rest mass of baryons relative to single quark knots.

Analogy (for intuition). Three equal water whirls feed one outlet: the hole may widen slightly, but the combined spin deepens the whirl and speeds the rim roughly threefold.

Mechanism: Shared Central Axis (Short-Range Coupling)

Two composite tubes (e.g., two protons) that share the same central line produce a combined circulation Γtotal=(3κ)proton+(3κ)proton=6κ, which deepens the shared pressure well. The velocity superposition gives vtotal=v1+v2⇒P∝−(v1+v2)2 The cross-term −2v1v2 deepens the local pressure well and yields attraction. With filamentary swirl vθ∝1/r, one has v1v2∝1/r2, hence Vint∝1/r2 and F=−∇Vint∝1/r3. This is consistent with short-range binding/flux-coupling, not gravity. This is consistent with the observation that neutral molecules (e.g., H2) attract in Euclidean space~[london1930], [casimirpolder1948]: their baryon cores can be connected by the same central line, with the resulting swirl contribution following from additive circulation.

Canonical reinterpretation: source vs field

Permanent exclusion: direct-line gravity.

The central-axis threading picture may be retained only as a local baryonic source-geometry and residual-coupling model. A literal vortex line connecting two separated masses behaves as a tension channel, not as a Newtonian 1/R2 force law. Its potential is confinement-like rather than gravitational, and it must not be used as the far-field gravity mechanism.

The knot/circulation content described in this document remains useful as a source specification (``what carries mass/charge''). In v0.6.1+, the field propagation responsible for 1/r tails is modeled by a mediator ϕ with static EFT Sstat[ϕ]=∫d3x[κ2(∇ϕ)2−λρm(x)ϕ],κ∇2ϕ=−λρm. The Green-function solution for a localized source yields ϕ(r)∝1/r, giving the correct inverse-square force.

Electromotive Response to Swirl Gravity

Recent work in the SST Canon~[Iskandarani2025EMG] indicates that time-dependent swirl density ∂tρ→↺ acts as a source term in a modified Faraday law: ∇×E→=−∂tB→−b→↺,b→↺=G↺∂tρ→↺ Here, G↺ is a universal topological transduction constant, canonically normalized to a flux quantum Φ⋆∈{h/e,h/2e}. For the formal derivation, see Appendix~sec:canonical-derivation-of-the-emswirl-coupling. This coupling leads to a falsifiable prediction: nucleation or reconnection of vortex lines produces a quantized electromotive impulse of magnitude Φ⋆. In gravitational contexts, pressure or density changes that alter swirl topology should have electromagnetic correlates. Thus, SST gravity is fluid-mechanical and electromagnetically active—features that can be tested in vortex-generating platforms.

Companion Paper Reference

The modified Faraday law~[Iskandarani2025EMG] with the swirl–induced source term~(eq:modified-faraday) is derived in a companion manuscript~[Iskandarani2025EMG]. There, it is shown that G↺ is quantized in Weber units and identified with a flux quantum~[DeaverFairbank1961], [LittleParks1962], G↺=Φ⋆∈{h/e,h/2e}. In the present work we focus on experimental implications.

Experimental Realization of Swirl-Induced ElectromotiveImpulses

Prediction

Topological transitions in the swirl sector (nucleation, annihilation, reconnection of swirl lines) generate quantized electromotive impulses, (6)ΔΦ=±Φ⋆,Φ⋆∈{he,h2e}, observable in any linked detection loop, independent of loop geometry. The sign of the impulse is set by chirality.

Condensed-Matter Implementation

Viable condensed-matter testbeds include:
  • Type-II superconducting thin films with vortex entry/exit control,
  • Quasi-2D atomic Bose–Einstein condensates,
  • Magnetic skyrmion or Hopfion films.
A lithographed multi-turn superconducting micro-coil is positioned such that the defect line threads the loop during a topological transition. The induced impulse voltage is (7)Vimp≈NΦ⋆Δt, where N is the number of turns and Δt is the event timescale.
Numerical example.
For N=1000, Φ⋆=h/2e≈2.07×10−15Wb, and Δt=10ns, Vimp≈0.207mV. For Δt=1ns, Vimp≈2.07mV.

Protocol and Statistics

  1. Prepare the platform under controlled (T,B,P).
  2. Trigger a single topological transition.
  3. Record the transient voltage.
  4. Repeat for 103–105 events.
  5. Histogram the normalized flux ∫V(t)dt/N.
Expected result: discrete peaks at integer multiples of Φ⋆, sign-flip under chirality reversal, invariance under linking-preserving deformations, collapse under unlinking or resistive replacement.

Hydrogenic and Atomic Systems

Swirl-Clock modulation predicts small line shifts in hydrogen, H−, and H2. High-resolution spectroscopy can be complemented with a micro-coil near the sample to detect coincident quantized impulses during internal topological transitions.

Falsifiability Criteria

  • Quantization: impulses in steps of Φ⋆,
  • Chirality: reversal flips sign,
  • Linking number protection: preserved under deformations, destroyed by unlinking,
  • Geometry independence: magnitude depends only on N and Δt.

Galactic Rotation and Dark Matter Analogue

In addition to the molecular-scale picture, applying the same circulation quantization at galactic scales yields a two-component rotation profile that can reproduce flattened curves without introducing a separate non-baryonic halo within this model. Let the azimuthal swirl velocity decompose into a core and a tail contribution: (8)vϕ(r)=vcore(r)+Ctail(1−e−r/rc), where vcore(r) arises from finite baryonic-core circulation and the second term represents saturation of swirl transmission into the disk.

Flat rotation curves.
In the limit r≫rc, Eq.~(eq:core-tail) asymptotes to vϕ(r)⟶Ctail, producing flattened rotation curves. This is a hydrodynamic consequence of circulation quantization and saturation in the present framework.
Finite energy density.
The swirl energy density associated with the tail is (9)ρE(r)=12ρfvϕ2(r)⟶12ρfCtail2(r→∞), which remains finite. Thus the apparent “dark halo” corresponds, in this model, to a constant swirl–energy plateau rather than an infinite mass distribution.
Chirality selection.
Following the chiral–achiral selection principle developed in earlier VAM work, only chiral knots couple coherently to the galactic swirl clock St↺. Achiral excitations (Fig.~fig:4-1) fail to bind and are repelled from high–vorticity regions, precluding virialized halos.
Rosetta consistency.
Using the Rosetta translation, the constants are fixed as ρf=ρcorerc‖v↺‖Ω,ρE=12ρf‖v↺‖2,ρm=ρE/c2, ensuring dimensional consistency across both atomic (hydrogen) and galactic (rotational) scales.
Falsifiers.
Two outcomes would challenge the proposal: (i) a system with well-measured baryons and negligible environmental coupling that still requires a full canonical dark-matter halo; (ii) a case where the inferred swirl coupling demands axis linkages that are topologically incompatible with the observed morphology.
Summary.
Equation~(eq:core-tail) provides a falsifiable, SST-specific analogue of dark-matter phenomenology: flat galactic rotation curves, finite halo energy, and chirality-restricted matter coupling arise from quantized circulation in flat space.

Entropic Embedding of Swirl–String Theory

Swirl–String Theory (SST), built on topologically quantized circulation in a flat, vortex-supporting medium, admits an entropic reinterpretation compatible with the core principles of emergent gravity [verlinde2011origin], [verlinde2016emergent], [jacobson1995thermodynamics], [padmanabhan2010thermodynamical], [bekenstein1973black], allowing mass, force, and time to be read as information-theoretic quantities.

Swirl Entropy as Informational Field

We define a swirl-based entropy field S(xμ)↺ as a logarithmic function of the swirl areal density ρ↺=∇⋅a→:

(10)S(xμ)↺=kB⋅log⁡(1+ρ↺(xμ)ρ0)

Here, ρ0 is a baseline density. The field S↺ plays the role of a local entropy density, similar to that on a holographic screen in entropic gravity.

Entropic Force from Swirl Gradients

Verlinde’s entropic-force expression is:

(11)F=T⋅dSdx

In SST, circulation-induced pressure deficits are (12)Δp=−12ρfv2

Assuming that swirl flow aligns with the entropy gradient, the effective force becomes (13)Fswirl∝∇(ρfv2)∝∇S↺, establishing an explicit analogy between entropic forces and swirl-induced attraction in SST.

Mass as Topological Information

In SST, a mass scale is set by the circulation quantum κ:

(14)m=hκ,κ=2πrcvc

Interpreting κ as a unit of quantized topological information, one may write a discrete sum over informational elements:

(15)mK=∑iϵi,ϵi=hκi.

Time Dilation as an Entropic Clock

SST defines a Swirl Clock for local proper time,

(16)dtlocal=dt∞1−v2c2,

consistent with entropic gravity, where time slows in regions of higher information density, i.e., larger ρ↺.

R/T Phase Transition and Information Localization

SST posits two phases:
  • R-phase: unknotted, wave-like field state
  • T-phase: knotted, particle-like topological excitation
The R-to-T transition represents entropic localization, akin to wavefunction collapse and decoherence, aligning SST with entropy-based emergence of space and matter.

Summary of Mapping

SST may therefore be read as an entropic field theory in flat space, where gravitational and inertial phenomena track topological and informational structures.

Lagrangian and Action Formulation

The dynamical content of Swirl–String Theory (SST) can be expressed via an effective Lagrangian density L over flat spacetime, with swirl fields defined by a scalar potential ϕ(xμ), a swirl vector potential aμ(xν), and a fluid mass density field ρf. Define the swirl areal density as ρ↺=∇⋅a→. With a Maxwell-like field strength Fμν=∂μaν−∂νaμ, a representative Lagrangian is LSST=−14FμνFμν+ρf(∂μϕ)(∂μϕ)−V(ϕ)+Ltopo, where V(ϕ) encodes a knot potential and Ltopo collects topological couplings (e.g., braid index, genus).

The action is then S=∫LSSTd4x. Euler–Lagrange equations yield conservation laws and dynamics for both swirl flow and its entropic analogs.

In hydrogenic systems, swirl gradients around knot cores induce pressure deficits that couple to particle motion via Bernoulli–Euler dynamics, reproducing an effective gravitational behavior without spacetime curvature.

The quantized vortex mass formula, the swirl Schrödinger equation, and finite-core energy regularization were developed in the VAM framework~[Iskandarani, 2024]. The present work translates and updates these within SST notation via the Rosetta map~[Iskandarani, 2025].

Legacy Foundations and Rosetta Translation

The formal structure of Swirl–String Theory (SST) builds on a prior topological-fluid framework, the Vortex–Æther Model (VAM). That model derived physical results from circulation quantization and fluid field dynamics, including a topologically quantized mass formula, a swirl-based Schrödinger equation, and a non-divergent fluid Lagrangian. These are translated within SST via a symbolic mapping documented in the Rosetta file [VAM-15], [vamrosetta2025].

Quantized Circulation and Mass Formula

In VAM, a core-mass mechanism arises from Onsager-like circulation quantization~[onsager1949], [feynman1955]: (17)∮v→⋅dℓ→=nκ\ae with velocity expressed as a gradient, (18)v→=λ\ae∇θ,ψ=ρ/ρ\aeeiθ, leading to a hydrodynamic Schrödinger equation with a swirl potential, (19)iℏ\ae∂ψ∂t=−ℏ\ae22m\ae∇2ψ+Φswirl(ω→)ψ, (20)Φswirl=12λgρ\ae|ω→|2.

Reported vortex-mass estimates (e.g., for the electron) were within ∼10−7 of experimental values in that framework; independent verification is an open task.

Lagrangian and Field Formalism

VAM provided a fluid Lagrangian consistent with gauge-invariant dynamics: (21)LVAM=12ρf(∇×A→)2+ρf(∂tϕ)2−V(ϕ). This maps to the SST flat-space field theory as (22)LSST=−14FμνFμν+ρf(∂μϕ)(∂μϕ)−V(ϕ)+Ltopo, where the swirl vector aμ replaces the VAM circulation potential, and Ltopo incorporates topological invariants (braid index, genus, component count).

Notation Fidelity via Rosetta Map

All constants, fields, and structural equations have been translated via the VAM–SST Rosetta dictionary [vamrosetta2025], maintaining dimensional and symbolic consistency. This includes:
  • Swirl velocity: v→↺=∇ϕ
  • Core swirl speed: ‖v→↺‖=1.093×106 m/s
  • Core radius: rc=1.40897×10−15 m
  • Core density: ρcore=3.89×1018 kg/m3
  • Time variables: external time τ, swirl clock S(t), and proper loop time Ts
This lineage yields a variational, quantized, and empirically calibrated foundation—recast here in a swirl-theoretic, flat-space field formalism.

Conclusion

Long-distance attraction in SST is a manifestation of topological quantization: chiral knots with central holes enforce non-vanishing circulation residues along a central line. When multiple quark knots merge into a baryon, their circulations add linearly, forming a single composite tube with 3κ circulation. Two testable consequences follow: (1) discrete electromotive impulses of fixed magnitude ΔΦ=±Φ⋆ at topology changes; (2) a contribution to large-scale dynamics that flattens rotation curves in systems with axis linkages.

Code and Data Availability

All predictive simulations used in this paper are implemented in the open Python script SST_INVARIANT_MASS3.py, available on request or at Zenodo: \url{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17155854}

Canonical Derivation of the EM–Swirl Coupling (Summary from Canon)

This appendix summarizes the canonical derivation of the EM–swirl coupling as developed in the Swirl–String Theory Canon~[Iskandarani_SST_Canon_v0_5_9_2025]. The goal is to show how time–dependent swirl density enters Maxwell–Faraday dynamics as an additional source term.

Swirl areal density.
A coarse–grained swirl density ρ↺(x,t) is defined as the number of quantized swirl lines per unit area. Its flux through a surface S counts the number of vortex lines piercing S, Φ↺(t;S)=∫Sρ↺dA=N(S,t)∈Z. Conservation of circulation (Kelvin invariant) ensures that N is an integer topological quantity that can only change by nucleation, annihilation, or reconnection.Full derivation available in the supplemental Canon document~[Iskandarani_SST_Canon_v0_5_9_2025].
Modified Faraday law.
In a rotating–frame foliation, centrifugal and swirl–gravity effects unify into a single effective source b↺. The Maxwell–Faraday curl equation becomes ∇×E=−∂tB−b↺,b↺=G↺∂tρ↺. Here G↺ is a universal transduction constant with dimensions of Weber (V·s), so that b↺ has the same units as ∂tB (V·m−2).
Pillbox theorem.
Integrating over a surface S and a time interval [ti,tf] yields ∫titf∮∂SE⋅dℓdt=−ΔΦB(S)−G↺ΔN(S), where ΔΦB(S) is the magnetic flux change and ΔN(S) is the net change in vortex number through S. If the magnetic flux is held fixed, the time–integrated EMF reduces to a purely topological impulse proportional to ΔN.
Normalization.
The Canon’s “electron logic’’ identifies one topological event (ΔN=±1) with a single flux quantum Φ⋆. This fixes the constant to G↺=Φ⋆,Φ⋆∈{he,h2e}, with the choice depending on whether the medium supports single–charge or Cooper–pair transport. This establishes that every topological transition injects a quantized EMF–time impulse, independent of drive details or geometry.
Dimensional consistency.
Since [ρ↺]=m−2 and [∂tρ↺]=m−2s−1, multiplying by [G↺]=V·s yields [b↺]=V·m−2, consistent with [∂tB].

Rotating Frame and Flux Quantization

The rotating–frame derivation of the flux impulse is presented in full in the companion paper [Iskandarani2025EMG]. The result is that each topological transition generates a quantized time–integrated electromotive force: ∫V(t)dt=Φ⋆ΔN,Φ⋆∈{he,h2e}.

Physical interpretation.
This law states that the EMF–time impulse is determined solely by the change in swirl line number (ΔN) and the universal flux quantum Φ⋆. The magnitude is independent of the loop geometry, linking details, or the microscopic rate of the event. Only the sign (set by chirality) and the integer ΔN matter.
Experimental implications.
In condensed–matter systems, controlled vortex entry or exit should yield measurable EMF impulses in linked pickup loops. The predicted size is ∼0.1–1 mV for N=103 turns and nanosecond-scale transitions, well within reach of SQUID or GHz digitizer detection.
Cosmological scaling.
At galactic scales, swirl nucleation or reconnection events during mergers should produce transient electromagnetic signatures. Their quantized character provides a falsifiable link between laboratory measurements and astrophysical phenomena.
Falsifiability.

Key experimental discriminants are: (i) quantization in units of Φ⋆; (ii) chirality–dependent sign reversal; (iii) invariance under continuous loop deformations that preserve linking number; (iv) collapse of the signal if the loop is unlinked or resistive.

These criteria connect the theoretical derivation of the swirl–EMF coupling directly to measurable laboratory and astrophysical observables.

Summary of Key Points.
  • Each topological swirl transition yields an impulse EMF ΔΦ=±Φ⋆.
  • The signal is quantized, chirality-sensitive, and geometry-independent.
  • Predictions apply across lab-scale and cosmic scales.

Experimental Realization of Swirl-Induced ElectromotiveImpulses

Prediction

Topological transitions in the swirl sector (nucleation, annihilation, reconnection of swirl lines) generate quantized electromotive impulses, (24)ΔΦ=±Φ⋆,Φ⋆∈{he,h2e}, observable in any linked detection loop, independent of loop geometry. The sign of the impulse is set by chirality.

Condensed-Matter Implementation

Viable condensed-matter testbeds include:
  • Type-II superconducting thin films with vortex entry/exit control,
  • Quasi-2D atomic Bose–Einstein condensates,
  • Magnetic skyrmion or Hopfion films.
A lithographed multi-turn superconducting micro-coil is positioned such that the defect line threads the loop during a topological transition. The induced impulse voltage is (25)Vimp≈NΦ⋆Δt, where N is the number of turns and Δt is the event timescale.

For N=1000, Φ⋆=h/2e≈2.07×10−15Wb, and Δt=10ns, Vimp≈0.207mV. For Δt=1ns, Vimp≈2.07mV.

Protocol and Statistics

  1. Prepare the platform under controlled (T,B,P).
  2. Trigger a single topological transition.
  3. Record the transient voltage.
  4. Repeat for 103–105 events.
  5. Histogram the normalized flux ∫V(t)dt/N.
Expected result: discrete peaks at integer multiples of Φ⋆, sign-flip under chirality reversal, invariance under linking-preserving deformations, collapse under unlinking or resistive replacement.

Hydrogenic and Atomic Systems

Swirl-Clock modulation predicts small line shifts in hydrogen, H−, and H2. High-resolution spectroscopy can be complemented with a micro-coil near the sample to detect coincident quantized impulses during internal topological transitions.

The dynamical content of Swirl–String Theory (SST) can be expressed via an effective Lagrangian density L over flat spacetime, with swirl fields defined by a scalar potential ϕ(xμ), a swirl vector potential aμ(xν), and a fluid mass density field ρf. In hydrogenic systems, swirl gradients around knot cores induce pressure deficits that couple to particle motion via Bernoulli–Euler dynamics, reproducing an effective gravitational behavior without spacetime curvature.

Conclusion

Long-distance attraction in SST is a manifestation of topological quantization: chiral knots with central holes enforce non-vanishing circulation residues along a central line. When multiple quark knots merge into a baryon, their circulations add linearly, forming a single composite tube with 3κ circulation. Two testable consequences follow: (1) discrete electromotive impulses of fixed magnitude ΔΦ=±Φ⋆ at topology changes; (2) a contribution to large-scale dynamics that flattens rotation curves in systems with axis linkages.

Canonical Derivation of the EM–Swirl Coupling (Summary from Canon)

This appendix summarizes the canonical derivation of the EM–swirl coupling as developed in the Swirl–String Theory Canon~[Iskandarani_SST_Canon_v0_5_9_2025]. The goal is to show how time–dependent swirl density enters Maxwell–Faraday dynamics as an additional source term.

Swirl areal density.
A coarse–grained swirl density ρ↺(x,t) is defined as the number of quantized swirl lines per unit area. Its flux through a surface S counts the number of vortex lines piercing S, Φ↺(t;S)=∫Sρ↺dA=N(S,t)∈Z. Conservation of circulation (Kelvin invariant) ensures that N is an integer topological quantity that can only change by nucleation, annihilation, or reconnection.Full derivation available in the supplemental Canon document~[Iskandarani_SST_Canon_v0_5_9_2025].
Modified Faraday law.
In a rotating–frame foliation, centrifugal and swirl–gravity effects unify into a single effective source b↺. The Maxwell–Faraday curl equation becomes ∇×E=−∂tB−b↺,b↺=G↺∂tρ↺. Here G↺ is a universal transduction constant with dimensions of Weber (V·s), so that b↺ has the same units as ∂tB (V·m−2).
Pillbox theorem.
Integrating over a surface S and a time interval [ti,tf] yields ∫titf∮∂SE⋅dℓdt=−ΔΦB(S)−G↺ΔN(S), where ΔΦB(S) is the magnetic flux change and ΔN(S) is the net change in vortex number through S. If the magnetic flux is held fixed, the time–integrated EMF reduces to a purely topological impulse proportional to ΔN.
Normalization.
The Canon’s “electron logic’’ identifies one topological event (ΔN=±1) with a single flux quantum Φ⋆. This fixes the constant to G↺=Φ⋆,Φ⋆∈{he,h2e}, with the choice depending on whether the medium supports single–charge or Cooper–pair transport. This establishes that every topological transition injects a quantized EMF–time impulse, independent of drive details or geometry.
Dimensional consistency.
Since [ρ↺]=m−2 and [∂tρ↺]=m−2s−1, multiplying by [G↺]=V·s yields [b↺]=V·m−2, consistent with [∂tB].

Rotating Frame and Flux Quantization

The rotating–frame derivation of the flux impulse is presented in full in the companion paper [Iskandarani2025EMG]. The result is that each topological transition generates a quantized time–integrated electromotive force: ∫V(t)dt=Φ⋆ΔN,Φ⋆∈{he,h2e}.

Physical interpretation.
This law states that the EMF–time impulse is determined solely by the change in swirl line number (ΔN) and the universal flux quantum Φ⋆. The magnitude is independent of the loop geometry, linking details, or the microscopic rate of the event. Only the sign (set by chirality) and the integer ΔN matter.
Experimental implications.
In condensed–matter systems, controlled vortex entry or exit should yield measurable EMF impulses in linked pickup loops. The predicted size is ∼0.1–1 mV for N=103 turns and nanosecond-scale transitions, well within reach of SQUID or GHz digitizer detection.
Cosmological scaling.
At galactic scales, swirl nucleation or reconnection events during mergers should produce transient electromagnetic signatures. Their quantized character provides a falsifiable link between laboratory measurements and astrophysical phenomena.
Falsifiability.

Key experimental discriminants are: (i) quantization in units of Φ⋆; (ii) chirality–dependent sign reversal; (iii) invariance under continuous loop deformations that preserve linking number; (iv) collapse of the signal if the loop is unlinked or resistive.

These criteria connect the theoretical derivation of the swirl–EMF coupling directly to measurable laboratory and astrophysical observables.

Summary of Key Points.
  • Each topological swirl transition yields an impulse EMF ΔΦ=±Φ⋆.
  • The signal is quantized, chirality-sensitive, and geometry-independent.
  • Predictions apply across lab-scale and cosmic scales.
